newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Virgin says plans major S.African investment.
newsitem.headline: Virgin says plans major S.African investment.

text.p: British entrepreneur Richard Branson said on Thursday his new Virgin Atlantic Airways service from London to Johannesburg would open the way for the rest of his retailing and entertainment empire to move into South Africa.
Branson told Reuters during the inaugural South African flight that plans were in hand to open up Virgin Megastores selling books, games and records.

He said that he also intended to serve the local airwaves with a new radio station and supply the nation's palate with Virgin Cola and Virgin Vodka, as well as appealing to the financially prudent with Virgin Direct which sells insurance and savings schemes.
"We are planning a major investment strategy in South Africa," he said. "We plan to follow with record shops, with Virgin Cola, and with our modelling agency," Branson added.

"Our record company is going to be setting up in South Africa, we have got together with Soweto Radio and applied for a licence to launch Virgin Radio and we are also looking at the possibility of doing a Virgin Cinema complex."

He later told a news conference that he expected the first South African Virgin Megastore would be in place within the next 12 months and within the next two years was looking at a total investment in the order of $100 million.
"But that's a very round figure," he said.
